vulnerabilities.description: normalizedLevel applies Number.isSafeInteger only to string-derived levels; its numeric branch accepts any finite integer >= 0. A hostile response with level greater than Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER therefore passes validation and is merged/navigated under an imprecise owner-cell key, despite seq now being safely bounded.

The lookup timeout races the read promise but does not abort or cancel the underlying resourceRead/fetch. Logical capacity and metrics are released after 10 seconds while the original network operation may remain unresolved; repeated timeout/TTL cycles can accumulate orphaned requests, sockets, and promise reactions outside the advertised active cap.

edgeCasesMissed: Reject numeric levels above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER exactly as string levels are rejected.
Abort the underlying point-read transport on timeout or prove a hard transport deadline; releasing only the logical in-flight slot does not bound unresolved network work.
After timeout, resolve the original read with a valid claim and assert it cannot merge, navigate, notify, alter caches, or change active/completed metrics a second time.
Exercise repeated timeout and retry cycles with permanently unresolved reads and assert the number of underlying reads remains bounded, not merely navigator.metrics().active.
Server integration remains unavailable in this restricted environment because Bun.serve cannot bind port 0; 21 focused browser tests and all 67 mcp-web unit tests pass.
topFinding: The current timeout bounds navigator bookkeeping but not the underlying resource operation, so indefinitely delayed reads can accumulate beyond the 16-slot cap; numeric levels also retain an unsafe-integer validation bypass.

impact.rationale: These are continuable projection-integrity and resource-bounding failures, not deterministic application crashes or core graph breaks. Generation-local capacity, stale-result suppression, safe seq validation, domain separator/control rejection, toast reset, tenant-scoped exact lookup, ambiguous query rejection, path redaction, bounded draft parsing, pagination isolation, aggregate identifier-free metrics, and no snapshot fallback otherwise hold.
